utterances.text: Now, we can go back a page, but the order includes a lot of details of where the various units involved in this operation, what axis they were going to be at, details of which you would accept are important for you as a communications officer to be aware of; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. However, we communicated with those units using radios with whip antennas, and these antennas beam in all directions equally. So wherever those units were located and regardless of their deployment, with that type of communication, I can more easily communicate with them. It is true that even for that type of communication it's important for me to know these units' axis of attack, whether they are on a clearing or a hilly or mountainous area so that I should know how the signals would spread. However, with all my prior experience, all these details were not crucial for the execution of that operation. The main thing for me to know was which units would be participating.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And it's clear that you hadn't informed your superior command that you had already set up communications at the Krivace forward command post; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which superior command do you mean now? When you say "my superior command"?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, your superior command. So General Krstic, the Chief of Staff, was not informed that you had already set up the communications at the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've told you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can I ask where that is in the document? Because I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see. Did you refer to a document?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then I'd ask for the reference from the question at line 24 for "it's clear that." "It's clear that" implies that it's in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily. The witness may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My Chief of Staff, General Krstic, at the joint meeting on the 11th of July, clearly heard where the forward command post of the Drina Corps would be for the Zepa operation, and he clearly heard when I was ordered to go there and set up a communications centre. For us soldiers, that is, quite simply, the beginning and the end of it all. It doesn't cross anybody's mind to go into any kind of unnecessary formality at moments like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Trivic recorded in his diary that at that meeting that you claim you attended on the night of the 11th, he had ordered -- Mladic -- General Mladic had ordered Krstic to produce "this attack order tomorrow," and I put it to you that that could only have occurred on the 12th of July which is why General Krstic issued this order, the attack order, on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are absolutely not right. I remember that this order was written by Colonel Vicic, operations officer in the Drina Corps, and for the entire day, the previous day, he was writing this order and he was waiting for General Krstic to sign it. Because I was waiting for all of them up there for two days since I was at the IKM already on the 12th and the units were relocated from the area of Srebrenica during the night between the 13th and the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's move on. On the night of the 11th when you claim you travelled to this meeting, you moved with all of your communications personnel in a large military communications truck; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, except for one soldier who was with General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And what was his name?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Plakalovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And according to you, you left Pribicevac for Bratunac via Potocari; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You passed through Potocari without an escort.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, I put it to you that there's no way you would have travelled through Potocari on the night of the 11th in a VRS military truck. I put it to you that the offensive was still going on and that Potocari had not yet been taken by the VRS, and therefore you could not have possibly driven through there that night.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I should like to correct you. When I testified previously, I said that as soon as night fell, I passed through Srebrenica and Potocari; that is to say, it wasn't night-time. It was just as night was falling. That is when the day turns into the night. So I know that our units had orders not to enter Potocari, or quite simply as they were going after the 28th Division, that should not be the point where they should focus. However, from communications, I had knowledge that the road from Srebrenica via Potocari to Bratunac was accessible because that is the main road and definitely the shortest road to Bratunac, and I set out through Potocari because I had an officer 's idea that this unit -- this area had been left by the units of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, when you passed through Potocari, you saw crowds of civilians, you saw UN DutchBat officers, and you saw members of the VRS; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I stated that during some of my previous testimony, that I saw lots of people, and this left a particular impression on me, a strange impression, as to all the things that war can produce. However they were they were intermingled, the population and UNPROFOR, so I can just tell you about what I saw along the main road that I was going down. I didn't stop but I saw lots of people. I saw members of UNPROFOR, they were all mixed, and in my assessment I saw a few members of the Army of Republika Srpska. Now, I don't know from which unit they were, but it remained in my mind that they were talking to the people there, so then I thought that they may have been soldiers from the surrounding villages who perhaps knew someone and therefore talked to them, so they were holding their rifles on their shoulders. A few of them. I saw a few of them as I was passing there, and I said that during every one of my previous testimonies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one clarifying question. You said in the area of Potocari, the units of the 28th Division had left already. Was that true for the whole of the route you took?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So no units of the 28th Division nearby the road you used.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's have a look at P02117.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: What we'll see here is the RS MUP special police brigade report. And it's from the deputy command, Deputy Commander Ljubisa Borovcanin. And he's writing to the Pale police staff sector and others, reporting on the activities of the RS MUP combat unit on 12 July 1995. You see the report, it's dated 13 July 1995. And he reports here that: "During the course of 12 July, MUP units were engaged in offensive actions from the direction of Zuti Most towards Potocari. At 0530 hours, we sealed off the check-point at Zuti Most and then proceeded along the road toward Potocari. There was no strong armed resistance from the Muslims, so we took control of Potocari by 1300 hours, and with a right hand flank we took control of the Budak and Milacevici features." Sir, you wouldn't have passed through Potocari when combat was still going on, would you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information I had and on the basis of which I made this assessment in terms of whether I could take that road or not, spoke in favour of that. Namely, that the 28th Division left its own civilians in Potocari and that they started their breakthrough towards Tuzla and that they were grouping in the part of the enclave towards Konjevic Polje. It is absolutely illogical that any one of them had the intention to stay that close to that road after I passed that way. And to this day I believe that was quite a risk on my part. So sometimes we'd talk to colleagues, officers, and, for example, I even received information stating that Vinko Pandurevic, commander of the Zvornik Brigade, as he went to that meeting he passed through Potocari. But when he saw what he saw, he went back taking a different route via Sas when going to Zeleni Jadar. But I really don't see what this document specifically says refuting what I have been saying so far. I can guarantee and I assert that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't have to bother about to what extent it supports or not. If you just answer the questions and tell us about what you know or what you -- what you considered at that time, you don't have to enter into a comparison of your own thoughts and what is written down here unless specifically asked. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, you don't contest then, as I understand it, that Potocari had not been taken at the time, sorry, that you claim to have passed through it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I passed through Potocari, there were no members of the 28th Division in Potocari. There were only civilians there, mixed with UNPROFOR, and a few members of the Army of Republika Srpska. Not a single member of the 28th Division was in Potocari at that point in time because then they were far to the west as they were regrouping for their breakthrough towards Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: What information did you have that informed you that it was safe for you to pass through Potocari?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Already in the afternoon, sometime when NATO air force struck, at the forward command post, we had a radio intercepting group of the Drina Corps that monitored the communications of the 28th Division. Already then in the afternoon of the 11th of July, we had information that their main plan was that civilians should go to the UNPROFOR base in Potocari and that they should group in the western part of the enclave, the 28th Division, that is, and that they should get ready for a breakthrough to join their main force in Tuzla and their auxiliary forces towards Zepa. So they had the entire afternoon to carry out this regrouping. So I absolutely had that information, and that was my assessment, that the 28th Division was no longer there on that road that I had intended to take.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, I'm looking at the clock. Would it be time for a break?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, that's appropriate. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you may follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I was a bit embarrassed that before the break I'd forgotten that you'd asked for a matter to be raised in private session. Should that be with or without the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Without.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Without the witness. Then we briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan, if you're ready you may continue once the witness has put on his earphones again.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: When you travelled -- when you left Pribicevac and travelled down to Srebrenica to pass through Potocari to get to Bratunac, did you pass any check-points?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I passed through an area that is called Tucak, I think where there used to be an UNPROFOR check-point.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did you pass through a check-point at Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did pass the check-point at Zuti Most, and over there there were a few soldiers, I think from the Bratunac Brigade, or policemen and so on. Somebody was there at that check-point. Before that operation was carried out, they had been there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I seek clarification of the previous answer. You said you "passed through an area that is called Tucak, I think where there used to be an UNPROFOR check-point." The question was whether you passed any check-points. Did you pass at Tucak any check-point; and, if so, manned by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the Prosecutor asked about the check-point in Zuti Most that was held by members of the Army of Republika Srpska. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that was her last question. The previous question was when you travelled -- when you left through Pribicevac and travelled down to Srebrenica to pass through Potocari to get to Bratunac, did you pass any check-points. That was the question. And then you told us that there was a place where there used to be an UNPROFOR check-point, but you did not answer the question whether there was a check-point at the time when you passed, and I was seeking clarification of that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that moment, it was not manned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So, Witness, then let's first deal with the Zuti Most check-point.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's look at P00724. Could we go to page 3 in the B/C/S and page 2 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And under the heading "12 July," if we scroll down a little bit in the English, I'm -- it reads in the second-to-last paragraph, second-to-lasts line: "The first task" -- and I don't know if can you see that in the B/C/S. Let me double-check for you. Yes. "The first task - to take control of the UN check-point on Zuti Most - was completed successfully without any incidents. The Dutch UN members did not react." Now this is a MUP report on the combat engagement of the special police brigade and other police in Srebrenica 1995, and it's a report Ljubomir Borovcanin dated -- he wrote about the events between 11 and 21 July 1995 and the report itself is dated 5 September 1995. So according to him, the UN were manning the check-point at Zuti Most and it was only on 12 July that they successfully took over control of that check-point. Do you contest that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you, please, in the Serbian version -- I haven't got the 12th. I just have the 13th. So could you please tell me which paragraph that is under that date so that I could read it?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes. If you look at the top of the Serbian version, you see it begins -- should begin "between 0500 and 0630 hours," and look -- and I don't read Cyrillic, but towards the end of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a bit unclear whether that's a new paragraph or the end of the first paragraph. There is a bit of -- Sir, the two lines following the first paragraph which consists of some eight lines, and then we have two paragraphs. That was the paragraph Ms. Hasan was reading from. And that details with the 12th of July. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you are reading out is not written here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You can see in the brackets --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, look at the two lines following the first full paragraph. The first full paragraph starts with 05 to 6.30, that takes approximately -- not only approximately but exactly eight lines, and then the two following lines.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So, sir, you just testified and told this Chamber that you passed the check-point at Zuti Most where there were members of the Bratunac Brigade or other VRS members, and Borovcanin is reporting here that that check-point hadn't been taken control of until the 12th of July. So is Borovcanin providing false information in his report?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that on that road I just came across members of the Army of Republika Srpska who were on the road towards Potocari and Srebrenica from Bratunac and that I passed by them. The entire road had not been blocked by any kind of fortification obstacles. It was free, this road, and I just passed there. I didn't stop. And to tell you the truth, I don't remember having seen members of UNPROFOR on that road.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, let's move, then, to see what members of DutchBat say about who was on that road on the night of the 11th. And I'll read you an excerpt from DutchBat officer Lieutenant-Colonel Alko Koster testimony in the Krstic case.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. I stand corrected. It's Lieutenant Koster, not Lieutenant-Colonel Koster. And I'll read that excerpt. He is asked about Potocari on the 11th of July. If we could have a look at 65 ter 32024.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I will read this to you so you can follow along: "Q. And what hours were you on duty in the [sic] area on the afternoon/evening of 11 July [sic]." This is line 3. "A. Eleventh. From the 11th, the afternoon, sir, I was on duty until approximately 8.00 p.m. and then I went up to the compound for approximately two hours, and then returned to my position, where I stayed the whole night, the morning, the afternoon of the 12th of July, and also the evening of the 12th of July." And I'll just skip a few lines to line 13. And, sir, I understand you speak English, if you wish you can also follow the transcript. "Q. Now, while you were gone from the area briefly on the evening of the 11th, did you have a deputy that was in command while you were gone? "A. Yes, sir, he was. "Q. And to your knowledge, on the afternoon or evening hours of July 11th, was there any vehicular traffic from the VRS military along that road? "A. No, sir. I have not seen any vehicle movement, VRS vehicle movement on that road, and neither I was reported to by my deputy on the 11th of July. "Q. Was there some kind of roadblock or check-point there? "A. Yes. We installed sort of a roadblock to guide and to guard the refugees, so a vehicle couldn't get through without being reported to me, without being seen by me."

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if we turn to the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: "Q. Would this have been a significant event if a VRS vehicle had come through this area on July 11th? "A. Yes, sir. "Q. Did you notice any VRS soldiers in this area around where the people are, or anywhere around this compound, around this road, on the afternoon or evening of July 11th? "A. Not on the [sic] -- not on July 11th, sir. "Q. Would that have been a significant event if VRS soldiers had been amongst the [sic] people or in this area? "A. Yes, sir. I would have seen them, I would have been reported, and also I guess the refugees would have panicked. So it's not been reported and I have not seen them. "Q. Can you be sure that no VRS vehicle came through this area and no VRS soldiers were in this area" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: "And no" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'll start that question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: "Q. Can you be sure that no VRS vehicle came through this area and no VRS soldiers were in this area on the evening or afternoon of July 11th? "A. Yes, I'm sure about it, on the 11th; yes, sir." So, Witness, do you also claim that Lieutenant Koster is wrong about that?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is not right because at the time when I passed there -- well, he himself says in that statement of his that you read out that he had left that point at 8.00 and that he stayed for two hours. I said in my statement that I passed there around 2100 hours, whereas he left around 2000 hours and he was away for two hours so he could not have seen me. Even had he been there. So I'm absolutely certain that I did pass that way, and he himself says in his statement that at the time when I passed there he was absent from that point. There's something else I wish to add here. Maybe for them it would be illogical to expect a military vehicle of the Army of Republika Srpska to pass along that road from the direction of Srebrenica. It would have been of interest to them that if vehicles from Bratunac were passing in the other direction towards Srebrenica. At any rate, when I passed there, he was not there, and he could not have seen me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, he is wrong, we do understand your answer. You're explaining why he is wrong. And then you select part of that statement. Now, if you wish to do that, that's fine. But he talked about being replaced and a deputy there, et cetera. So you're not here to argue and to tell him why he is wrong and what may have been on their mind. You just say he is making a mistake. And that's -- because if you start explaining, then, of course, if you already do that and you're not invited to do that, but then take all of the information in the statement into consideration and not just the part you selected. This is not argument. This is testimony. Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's move on a little. The communications centre that you set up at the forward command post for the Krivaja 95 operation, now that communication centre was basically mounted on a truck; that's right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And within that vehicle, you had the means to establish communications between -- sorry. You had the means to establish communications with subordinate units of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both subordinate and superiors.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And in that vehicle, you had an RRU-1 device; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, the members of your unit that were with you at this communications centre, that included Oliver Sekulic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Momir Bakmaz.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bakmaz, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I apologise for my pronunciation. Veljko Vukosavljevic?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mirko Plakalovic.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you recall anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two or three more soldiers who were with me from the operation in Srebrenica, but I don't remember their names.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, you left Pribicevac at approximately 1900 hours, is that correct, on the 11th of July? That's what you claim?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you go --

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you continue -- you continue to Bratunac and sometime after midnight you arrive in Vlasenica; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, you didn't return to Pribicevac after that to set up communications again, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, in fact, all the components of the communications centre that you had which had been installed for the Krivaja 95 operation moved with you.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: What time on the 12th of July were communications -- was the communications centre at Krivace operational?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the early afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And when you moved with your vehicle, am I correct that the communications equipment in your vehicle was not functioning. It was disengaged?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not working.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So then from around 1900 hours on the 11th of July, which is when you claim you left Pribicevac, to the time you arrive in Vlasenica, until you set up communications the next day in Krivace, your communication centre, the Drina Corps IKM was out of operation.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: It was not possible during that time to communicate through a teleprinter, was it?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not possible to communicate through that teleprinter that was used at the IKM.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we could have a look at 65 ter 4399, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And what you see here is an 11 July Drina Corps order to block the linking up of the forces of the 28th enemy division with the forces in the enclaves. And it is addressed to a number of commands, including the Drina Corps IKM. You see that there?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And it is marked "very urgent." Now, this is an order from --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we turn to the last page.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Signed for General Zivanovic. And we see here a received stamp, and it's dated 11 July, 2230 hours, processed 11 July, 2250 hours. And am I correct that this means the cryptographer received this document at 2230 hours, he processes it at 2250 hours, and then it gets sent; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He encrypted it up to 2250. Out of that entire telegram, he made an encrypted tape ready for transmission.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd offer 65 ter 4399 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7131, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we have a look at now D00289, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And we see here this is a very urgent 11 July order to block the linking up of the forces of the 28th enemy division with the forces in the enclaves, the same order we saw before. And it's a teletyped version.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if we turn to the next page, we see that in handwriting it says "received, 11 July 1995 at 2350." It has a number and it bears a signature. Do you recognise that signature.

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So according to this document, which is addressed to the Drina Corps IKM, it was received on 11 July at 2350 hours when you claim the communications centre of the forward command post was completely disengaged. Now, I first want to ask you a question about this handwriting. Was it normal at the IKM to -- to write it this way as opposed to the previous document where we saw a stamp. Was that the typical way you noted that a telegram had been received?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because at the IKM, sometimes we didn't have the usual stamp.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And at the Pribicevac -- when the IKM was at Pribicevac, sir, you did not have that stamp, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that detail because only the encryptor does such things, but I think we didn't have that stamp.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I take it that you take the position that this document which is dated 11th July, 2350, was not received at the Drina Corps IKM as is indicated here?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. That's my position.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And the reason you claim that you dismantled the communications centre at the forward command post is because, in your assessment, the combat was over, you had precise knowledge, information, about where the 28th Division was moving, and, therefore, you decided to pick up and go. Did you receive any orders to move the IKM?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made my own assessment. Considering that the combat disposition had gone forward and my commander, the commander who was commanding that operation, was very busy with that operation, I decided I would be more useful to him if I followed. Because when the combat lines move forward, the communications centre has to move forward too. And the IKM has to move. I supposed that the commander had forgotten to order me to move the forward command post, and I decided to follow him and follow the combat lines. That's the reason I packed up my equipment and headed forward.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: The intelligence that you had, you said you received from a radio reconnaissance platoon. Now, the 4th Reconnaissance Platoon was located just about 100 or so metres from the forward command post. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One group of intercepters from that platoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And it was on the basis of information that they had gathered that you understood -- well, that they knew where the 28th Division was and, on that basis, you decided to move. That's correct?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only based on that information.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, what other information did you have; and from whom?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had information from the units that were in contact with the enemy. That means the units who were in direct fire contact from the enemy. From them, we knew where the enemy was exactly. And the other information we gathered from intercepts.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So let's take a look at 65 ter 04147.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Should we do that today or should we do that after today?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I would prefer to do it today, but I'll leave it your hands, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, how much time would that take? I can imagine that sometimes there's a good reason to just conclude a certain portion of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: It's just a question of pulling up the document, I'll briefly explain what it is, and have the witness comment on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have only a couple of minutes. That would be sufficient?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I think it's manageable. I hope so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I would agree. And with the assistance of all those in the booth, you may proceed for those few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: This is an interim report from the 4th Radio Reconnaissance Platoon. It's dated the 12th July, and it is passing on information intelligence department, Drina Corps intelligence section -- department. And it's addressed to the Drina Corps Pribicevac forward command post. This is processed by teleprinter; right?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you'd agree that that's the signature of (redacted) on that document?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And in handwriting, it says "received 12 July at 0740 hours." And it provides: "Commanders and signalsmen, by monitoring this network, we reached the conclusion that they were all present ..." And I'll pause there, "they" being in the previous paragraph it explains Naser's men. And it continues: "That they were heading in a direction unknown to us yet together with the people ... and their groups." You see that there? So how is it possible, sir, that the intelligence being received by the 4th Reconnaissance Platoon was indicating to the Drina Corps Command intelligence department that they -- there was no information about where the 28th Division was? And so I put it to you that, in fact, there was no information to the knowledge of the Drina Corps at that moment about the whereabouts of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: MILENKO JEVDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is information from only one group of interceptors. The radio reconnaissance platoon of the Drina Corps had several intercepting groups in its area of responsibility, and during the execution of the Srebrenica operation, it sent one intercepting group to the centre at Pribicevac. I received information - and not only I - from that group. This report contains information collected by a different intercepting group in a totally different part of the Drina Corps area of responsibility, and you see that reference is made here to Naser's people. Naser, at that time, was in Tuzla, not with the 28th Division. This is information from a different intercepting group, not the one at Pribicevac. And I sincerely hope that somebody will ask me how it is possible that this telegram was received on 12 July at Pribicevac where I maintain there was no communications centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you tendering this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, I will do that now then. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7132, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. P7132 is admitted, under seal; and P7131 is to be put under seal as well. We adjourn for the day. Witness, I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone or communicate in any way with whomever about your testimony. We have no court hearing tomorrow, so therefore we'd like to see you back on Monday morning at 9.30 again. And I take it, Ms. Hasan, then we'll easily conclude the testimony by that day. I'm also looking at Mr. Ivetic. We'd like to see you back then.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure that it's necessary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we move into private session, because you were uncertain about whether it has to be under seal. Is that the issue?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we move into private session very briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume on Monday, the 23rd of February, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 23rd day of February, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.24 p.m.,
